newsitem.title: USA: TWA February load factor rises to 63.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: TWA February load factor rises to 63.5 pct.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc on Wednesday said its February load factor was higher than it was a year ago, even though a reduction in flights to make more aircraft available for maintenance lowered capacity and passenger traffic during the period.
The company said its load factor rose to 63.5 percent from 61 percent in February 1996.
Available seat miles fell to 2.6 billion from 2.9 billion, while the carrier's total revenue passenger miles slipped to 1.6 billion from 1.8 billion.
TWA said the substitution of smaller, more efficient aircraft contributed to the drop in available seeat miles.
TWA said it typically reduced overall flying in winter months but this year took more airplanes out of service than usual in anticipation of heavy spring and summer schedules.
The carrier said noted that 1996 was a leap year, with 29 days in February, compared with 28 days this year.
